info.description:
Campus API for managing educational resources.

## Error Responses

All error responses follow a consistent envelope format. See the `ErrorEnvelope` schema for details.

## Error Codes

Common error codes:
- `INVALID_REQUEST` (400): Malformed or invalid request
- `UNAUTHORIZED` (401): Missing or invalid authentication
- `FORBIDDEN` (403): Insufficient permissions
- `NOT_FOUND` (404): Resource not found
- `VALIDATION_FAILED` (422): Request validation failed with field-level errors
- `CONFLICT` (409): Resource state conflict
- `INTERNAL_ERROR` (500): Unexpected server error
- `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (503): Required dependency is down; retry later


## Trailing slashes

Paths are listed exactly as routed (Flask): a path shown with a trailing slash must be requested with it — the no-slash variant answers with a 308 redirect.

put.description:
Every row is validated before any write, so a bad row anywhere
leaves the calendar untouched. Rows carrying a date that already
has a calendar row are updated in place; the rest are created.

Method:

Body Parameters:
    days: list[dict]
        Each row: {date (or id), j1_code?, j2_code?, term_week?} —
        codes from CALENDAR_CODE_VOCABULARY ("Mon A".."Fri B",
        "Free", "School Holiday", "Public Holiday", "Independent
        Learning Day") or null; `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`.

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        {"upserted": n, "days": [written rows, ordered by date]}.

    400 Bad Request: dict
        A malformed row, an unknown day code, or a duplicate date
        in the payload.

        A malformed date or an unknown day code.

    name: str (required)

    tag: CircleTag (required)
        The tag that categorizes the circle.

        Example:

                    "circle_1a2b3c4d": 15

    400 Bad Request: None
        Returned if the request body is invalid or missing required fields.

    409 Conflict: None
        - Returned if another circle already uses the requested name
          (best-effort, exact-match check).
        - Returned if tag is "root" and parents were provided.

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned if the caller is not a member of the
        `circles.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).

    422 Unprocessable Entity: None
        Returned if validation fails (e.g., a required field is missing).

post.description:
Add a member to a circle with a specified access level

Add a member to a circle with a specified access level.

Method:
    POST /circles/{circle_id}/members/add

Path Parameters:
    circle_id: str (required)
        The unique identifier of the circle to which the member will be added.

Query Parameters:
    None

Request Body (application/json):
    member_id: str (required)
        The member being added — circles contain only circles, so
        this is either a circle ID or the email name of the user's
        circle (each user has a circle named after their email
        account). The addressed circle must exist.
    access_value: AccessValue (required)
        The level of access the member will have in the parent circle.

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        Empty object indicating the member was successfully added.
        Example:
            {}

    409 Conflict: None
        - Returned if the target circle does not exist.
        - Returned if the member ID does not address an existing
          circle (including a missing user circle for an
          email-shaped ID).
        - Returned if no changes were applied (e.g., member already exists with same access).

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned if the caller is not a member of the
        `circles.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).

    500 Internal Server Error: None
        Returned if a storage-level error occurs during the operation.

Notes:
    - Emits the event: `campus.circles.members.add`.
    - Requires membership in the `circles.admin` circle: membership
      editing is privilege escalation once circles gate access.
    - Members are stored as a single `members` dict on the circle
      record, written by read-modify-write: member identifiers may
      be email names, whose dots a nested-field update path would
      misparse.

    404 Not Found: dict
        Unknown record.

    409 Conflict: dict
        The record is already effective, cancelled, or superseded.

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned if the caller is not a member of the
        `subjcombi.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).

get.description:
Resolves through the maintained mapping (its stored label
translated to a group id through the current timetable), then the
current timetable's file-derived roster, then unmapped. A mapping
whose label no current-timetable group carries is an orphan and
resolves as unmapped.

Method:
    GET /subjcombi/{user_id}

Query Parameters:
    at: str | None (optional)
        ISO datetime to resolve the mapping as of (default: now).

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        {"user_id": ..., "lessongroup_id": ... | null,
         "source": "mapping" | "roster" | "unmapped"}
get.summary: Get the user's effective subject-combination mapping.

put.description:
Appends an effective-dated record; the previous pending record
(if any) is superseded. Scheduled records take effect at their
`effective_from` without any scheduler process.

Method:
    PUT /subjcombi/{user_id}

Path Parameters:
    user_id: UserID
        The user whose mapping is set (their campus account email).

Body Parameters:
    lessongroup_id: CampusID
        The lessongroup to map the user to, by label (the v1
        ttcode, e.g. "2601-H1/P" or a bare class code "2607").
        Stored verbatim; it need not exist in any timetable yet —
        mappings populate ahead of the year's first upload, and
        the version-switch check highlights mappings whose label
        no uploaded timetable carries.
    reason: str | None (optional)
        Free-text change note, preserved on the trail record.
    effective_from: str | None (optional)
        When the mapping takes effect: ISO datetime, or
        `YYYY-MM-DD` for 07:00 school time on that date. Absent =
        immediate.

Responses:
    201 Created: dict
        The created trail record (includes
        `previous_lessongroup_id` and `actor_id`).

    400 Bad Request: dict
        Empty `lessongroup_id` or malformed `effective_from`.

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned if the caller is not a member of the
        `subjcombi.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).

get.description:
The deployment's current timetable and the pending switch, if any.
Pointers are an effective-dated trail: a scheduled switch flips as
a read-time fact at its effective_from.

Method:
    GET /timetable/

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        {"current": timetable_id | null, "next": timetable_id |
        null, "effective_from": datetime | null}
get.summary: Get the active-timetable pointer state.

patch.description:
Exactly one pointer key per call. `{current}` flips immediately
(trail row effective now). `{next, effective_from?}` schedules or
reschedules the pending switch — date-only values apply at 07:00
school time; an absent effective_from stages an undated switch
that flips only when pointed at manually. `{next: null}` cancels
the pending switch.

Method:
    PATCH /timetable/

Body Parameters:
    current: CampusID (alternative)
        The timetable ID to make current, effective now.
    next: CampusID | null (alternative)
        The timetable ID to schedule as the pending switch, or
        null to cancel the pending switch.
    effective_from: str | None (optional, with `next` only)
        When the pending switch applies.

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        The resulting pointer state (same shape as GET /timetable/).

    400 Bad Request: dict
        Both keys, unknown fields, `effective_from` without a
        `next` id, or a malformed `effective_from`.

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned if the caller is not a member of the
        `timetable.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).
patch.summary: Patch one timetable pointer: flip current or schedule next.

post.description:
Lessongroup ids are reused by label across allocations (#592):
a label that already has a group row — from any earlier allocation
— keeps its id, and the row moves to the new allocation, so
subjcombi mappings keyed by lessongroup_id survive version
switches. The payload shape is unchanged (label/members/entries).

Method:
    POST /timetable/

Body Parameters:
    metadata: dict
        Metadata for the timetable, e.g. start and end date.

    data: dict
        The actual timetable data, e.g. lesson groups and entries.

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
       {"data": timetable resource with labeled entries}

    400 Bad Request: dict
        {"error": error message} — missing 'lessongroups',
        missing group keys, or a label repeated within the
        payload (one label anchors one group).

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned if the caller is not a member of the
        `timetable.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).

    409 Conflict: dict
        A payload label is already claimed by two or more group
        rows — historical drift; clean up the duplicate-label
        rows and retry.

Method:

Query Parameters:

Responses:

get.description:
The subject is the bearer token's user — no user_id parameter.
The current leg resolves the active timetable version and the
user's effective subject combination (maintained mapping, else the
version's file-derived roster) at `at` (default now). The next leg
shows the state at the earliest pending change — a scheduled
version switch or the user's scheduled subjcombi record, whichever
comes first — with `change_type` telling the two planning cases
apart (whole-school vs affected-students-only). Entries are fetched
separately via /timetable/{id}/entries and filtered by
lessongroup_id.

Method:
    GET /timetable/me

Query Parameters:
    at: str | None (optional)
        ISO datetime to resolve the view as of (default now).

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        {"current": {timetable_id, lessongroup_id, source},
         "next": null | {timetable_id, lessongroup_id, source,
         effective_from, change_type: "timetable" | "subjcombi" |
         "both"}}

    401 Unauthorized: None
        No authenticated user.
get.summary: Resolve the signed-in user's effective timetable view (#592).

delete.description:
Cascades the version's entries, group members and lessongroup rows,
then the version itself. This is the cleanup surface for the
label-drift create 409: stale duplicate-label rows are owned by the
superseded versions that minted them, so deleting those versions
clears the drift. A group row that a later create reused is owned
by that later version and survives.

Refuses to delete the version the current or next pointer names —
move/cancel the pointer first. This action is destructive and
cannot be undone.

Method:
    DELETE /timetable/<timetable_id>/

Path Parameters:
    timetable_id: CampusID
        The ID of the timetable version to delete.

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        Empty JSON object indicating successful deletion.

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned if the caller is not a member of the
        `timetable.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).

    404 Not Found: dict
        {"error": error message} — unknown timetable_id.

    409 Conflict: dict
        {"error": error message} — the version is the current or
        next pointer target.
delete.summary: Delete a timetable version and all of its rows (#1088).

post.description:
The body is the raw file content; the `filename` query parameter
carries the committee's original filename (what the card shows)
and the Content-Type header is stored and served back. Each upload
mints a new attachment — re-uploading the same filename adds a
second copy rather than replacing one (removal is explicit).

Method:
    POST /timetable/<timetable_id>/attachments/

Path Parameters:
    timetable_id: CampusID
        The ID of the timetable.

Query Parameters:
    filename: str (required)
        The attachment's display filename.

Body:
    Raw bytes (any Content-Type; defaults to application/octet-stream).

Responses:
    201 Created: dict
        The attachment record (a files-backend record; the
        attachment id is the record's `id`).

    400 Bad Request: dict
        {"error": error message} — missing filename or empty body.

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned if the caller is not a member of the
        `timetable.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).

    404 Not Found: dict
        {"error": error message} — unknown timetable_id.
post.summary: Attach a file (PDF, image, …) to a timetable version.

attachment never touches the timetable itself.

        `timetable.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).

    404 Not Found: dict
        {"error": error message} — unknown id, or the attachment
        belongs to a different timetable.

patch.description:
A subset update: send any of `label`, `start_date`, `end_date` —
only the fields present in the body change. The label is the
committee's user-given display name (timetable-v2 Manage
Timetables); `null` clears it back to unnamed. `filename` is the
allocation's identity and is not updatable.

Method:
    PATCH /timetable/<timetable_id>/metadata

Path Parameters:
    timetable_id: CampusID
        The ID of the timetable.

Body Parameters:
    label: str | None (optional)
        The new display name, or null to clear it. An empty
        string is rejected — clear with null instead.
    start_date: DateTime (optional)
        The new start date of the timetable.
    end_date: DateTime (optional)
        The new end date of the timetable.

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        The updated metadata resource.

    400 Bad Request: dict
        {"error": error message} — empty body, unknown fields, a
        `filename` patch attempt, or an empty `label` string.

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned if the caller is not a member of the
        `timetable.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).
patch.summary: Update metadata fields for a specific timetable.
